clue.text: He said belts need to be adjusted and secured

indicators.note: letters that need adjusting are put into a fresh order, so the phrase is rearranged

explanation.surface: A man claims his belts must be tweaked before they are fastened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be adjusted' rearranges the eleven letters of HE SAID BELTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something established is set up firmly, fixed in place, made secure.

clue.text: Note goes to small house in London area

parts.note: so (soh) is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A memo is delivered to a modest home somewhere in London.
explanation.walkthrough: SOHO is a district of central London known for nightlife and theatres.
explanation.definitionFit: A named district of the West End of the capital.

clue.text: Possibly leaves without student for exams

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the shuffled letters go round the student
possibly signals that the letters of leaves could be arranged another way

parts.note: L is a learner, as on the L-plate of a learner driver

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone takes time off and skips the students' exams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges LEAVES; 'without' wraps that around L. A levels are the English school-leaving exams taken around age 18.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the Advanced-level qualifications sat in the final years of English secondary school.

clue.text: She's not improved by the golden touch

definitions.text: She's not improved by the golden touch

parts.words: She's not improved by the golden touch
parts.note: the saying that gilding a certain white flower is pointless overdoing, read as a woman's name who needs no gilding

explanation.surface: A woman whose beauty no gold leaf could enhance.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'gild the lily' is to try to improve what is already perfect; 'She' points to the girl's name too.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb about gilding this flower says adding gold spoils rather than improves it.

clue.text: Street names changed — they're a bit flowery

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: The road signs were renamed with something floral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges ST plus NAMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamens are the pollen-bearing male parts of a blossom, literally a bit of a flower.

clue.text: Always puts a woman right

parts.note: Eve is a woman's name, the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: Someone constantly sets a lady straight.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb meaning at all times, forever, as in 'ever after'.

clue.text: Spectators stand for this progressive movement

definitions.text: Spectators stand for this progressive movement

parts.words: Spectators stand for this progressive movement
parts.note: crowds in a stadium rise in turn so a ripple travels round the ground; 'progressive' means moving along, not politically radical

explanation.surface: Onlookers back a forward-thinking political cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stand for' sounds like 'support', and 'progressive movement' like politics; really the fans literally stand up in sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: The stadium ripple made by sections of fans standing and sitting in turn, popularised at the 1986 World Cup.

clue.text: Person with two hips?

parts.note: hips here are the shouts of 'hip, hip' before a hurrah, which a crowd leader calls out

explanation.surface: A question about someone's anatomy.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue seems anatomical, but 'hip, hip, hooray' is the cheer the leader leads.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who leads a crowd in rousing shouts such as 'hip, hip, hooray'.

clue.text: Rush to look after sister, perhaps?

parts.note: to charge is to rush at something
to nurse is to look after someone who is ill

explanation.surface: Hurrying off to care for one's female sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: In British hospitals a 'sister' is the senior nurse in charge of a ward, not a sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: Sister is the traditional British hospital title for a senior ward nurse, so a sister is an example.

clue.text: Salesman took exception to being substituted

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
to take exception to something is to resent it

explanation.surface: A travelling seller objected when he was replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: To be represented is to have someone stand in or act in your place.

clue.text: Mountaineer out for the count

indicators.note: out in the sense of wrong or disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A climber knocked unconscious by a blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of MOUNTAINEER; 'out for the count' borrows the boxing phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Enumeration is the act of counting or listing items one by one.

clue.text: Repeat after some reflection

parts.note: sound bouncing back off a surface gives a repetition; 'reflection' suggests thinking it over

explanation.surface: Say it again once you have had a think.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflection' looks like careful thought; it is sound waves bouncing back.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound reflected from a wall or cliff returns as a repeated copy.

clue.text: Sappers in control of cavalry

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the army corps whose soldiers are called sappers

explanation.surface: Army engineers take charge of the mounted troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap a rider uses to steer a horse, hence control of mounted soldiers.

clue.text: Airs composed by priest in Hebrew

indicators.note: composed in the sense of put together anew, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Bible who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: Melodies written by a clergyman in an ancient language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges AIRS to ISRA, then the biblical priest ELI is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebrew can mean a Jewish person, and a citizen of the Jewish state is one sense of it.

clue.text: Winter cover raised in freeze

parts.note: ice covers ponds and roads in winter
raised means up

explanation.surface: A frosty layer lifted during a cold snap.
explanation.definitionFit: To become clogged or coated with frozen water, as a windscreen or engine does.

clue.text: It makes the grandee angered and enraged

definitions.text: It makes the grandee angered and enraged

parts.words: It makes the grandee angered and enraged
parts.note: the three words grandee, angered and enraged share the same seven letters, each a rearrangement of the others

explanation.surface: Something infuriates the nobleman until he is furious.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks like a nobleman losing his temper; really it describes what turns one word into another.
explanation.definitionFit: A word made by rearranging the letters of another, as grandee becomes enraged.

clue.text: Sense of anxiety possibly nags the third mate

indicators.note: possibly signals another arrangement of the letters of nags
the third letter of the word mate is taken

explanation.surface: A worried feeling perhaps bothers one's third partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges NAGS into ANGS; 'the third' takes T from MATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst is a deep feeling of dread or unease.

clue.text: Looks over southern vessels

parts.note: cans are containers, i.e. vessels

explanation.surface: Someone inspects ships from the south.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan is to examine or glance over something quickly.

clue.text: Silver-headed editor, getting on a bit

indicators.note: headed means the silver piece goes at the top, before the editor

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A grey-haired newspaper editor is growing old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silver-headed' looks like grey hair; it puts AG at the head of ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderly, advanced in years, getting on as people say.

clue.text: He employs us with hesitation

parts.note: er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A boss hires us, though reluctantly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who uses something employs it, so the person who employs.

clue.text: Go to pieces, because of over-inflation?

definitions.text: Go to pieces, because of over-inflation?

parts.words: Go to pieces, because of over-inflation?
parts.note: an overfilled balloon or tyre splits open; 'go to pieces' and 'inflation' suggest a breakdown and an economy

explanation.surface: Someone cracks up under rising prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over-inflation' suggests economics, but it is a balloon blown up too far.
explanation.definitionFit: To split apart suddenly, as a balloon does when overfilled with air.

clue.text: Play truant when sleeping place not available

parts.note: a bunk is a narrow bed
off, as a dish is off the menu when it is not available

explanation.surface: A child skips school because there is no bed for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunk off' is British slang for skipping school or work.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for skiving, staying away from lessons without permission.

clue.text: Trooped out to see a naval weapon

indicators.note: out as in disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Soldiers marched off to view a warship's armament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TROOPED; 'to see' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-propelled underwater missile fired from a submarine or ship.

clue.text: Finished in a state of excitement

explanation.surface: Over and done with, yet all worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Ended (a meeting is wound up when concluded); and tense or agitated, like a coiled spring.

clue.text: Best way to secure a crest of hair

parts.note: top means best, as in top marks
a knot is a way of tying something fast

explanation.surface: The best method for fixing a tuft of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A bun or tuft of hair gathered on the crown of the head.

clue.text: Travel authority is located in Virginia

indicators.note: located in tells us one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: A permit for travel is found in a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: An endorsement on a passport giving permission to enter a country.

clue.text: It turns on an opponent

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed below the previous piece, so it comes after
turns means the word it is read backwards

explanation.surface: Something rounds on an adversary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' signals a reversal; in a down clue 'on' means placed beneath, so the reversed word follows the article. 'It turns on' reads like an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is against something, as in 'the antis'.

clue.text: A duck egg blue

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, from its egg-like shape, so it means nil

explanation.surface: The pale greenish-blue of a duck's egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck egg blue' is a real paint colour, misleading the solver. ANIL is the indigo plant and its dye.
explanation.definitionFit: Anil is the indigo shrub and the deep dye made from it.

clue.text: He is brave, so was she

definitions.text: He is brave, so was she

parts.words: He is brave, so was she
parts.note: a courageous man is called this, and it is also the name of the priestess in the Greek tale with Leander, who drowned herself for love

explanation.surface: A man is courageous, and so was a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek legend Hero was the priestess whose lover Leander swam the Hellespont nightly; she leapt to her death when he drowned.
explanation.definitionFit: A man admired for courage; also the legendary priestess loved by Leander.

clue.text: He's on about being present

parts.note: re means on or about, regarding

explanation.surface: A man going on about turning up.
explanation.definitionFit: Here describes being in this place, attending, as at a roll call.

clue.text: In the finish the teller with the key came across

indicators.note: In tells us the teller with the key goes inside the finish

parts.note: the finish is the end
a counter is one who counts, a teller
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: At the end, the bank teller holding the key showed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals a container: the teller and the key go together inside the finish. 'came across' reads as travelled over but means met.
explanation.definitionFit: To encounter is to meet by chance, to happen upon.

clue.text: Tour de France?

parts.note: in French tour also means tower, so this asks for the most famous tower in France rather than the cycle race

explanation.surface: The famous bicycle race.
explanation.walkthrough: The obvious reading is the cycle race; French 'tour' (feminine) means tower.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris landmark is the best-known tower in that country.
